domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: AI-first solutionism or value theatre
canonical_definition: AP-A2 examines whether commitment to AI preceded a defined technology-neutral problem and baseline, whether viable non-AI alternatives were bypassed, whether adoption or activity metrics substituted for outcome evidence, or whether progression continued after recorded results failed agreed conditions.
failure_mechanism: Pre-committed AI selection and activity/vanity reporting bypass technology-neutral problem framing, non-AI alternative comparison, total-cost accounting, and objective stop gates.
potential_consequences: Irreversible investment or deployment into an unsuitable or disproportionate AI mechanism
Activity or usage reporting masking negative net outcomes, human rework, or uncompensated risk
Continued progression or scaling after trial evidence breaches agreed stop thresholds

conditions: Applicable wherever AI is proposed, selected, funded, piloted, continued, scaled, or materially changed for an organizational, user, or societal outcome.
Check decision chronology, purchasing/delivery commitments, alternatives reviews, and actual gate decisions rather than retrospective summaries.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit AI-first solutionism or value theatre: AI is adopted for novelty, availability or signalling without evidence that it is the best proportionate mechanism.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show a predetermined AI solution, missing baseline comparison, or activity metrics substituting for value?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of AI-first solutionism or value theatre, or does it remain unknown?

atomic_tests.test: Trace the chronology of problem definition, AI selection, procurement, funding, metric design and approval to determine whether the mechanism was effectively predetermined.
Determine whether the stated problem and desired outcome remain meaningful and testable without referring to AI, a model, a vendor or technical capability.
Determine whether a current baseline, counterfactual and feasible non-AI or simpler alternatives were defined before the decision.
Test whether reported activity, usage, delivery, model or publicity metrics have an explicit causal and measurement link to the desired outcome and complete cost boundary.
Compare option assumptions and determine whether alternatives and proportionality were evaluated using consistent outcome, scale, cost, risk and lifecycle criteria.
Determine whether total cost, human workload, control burden, dependency, rights and risk evidence are materially omitted or minimized in the value case.
Review representative comparative results for selective reporting, post-hoc metric changes, excluded failures, subgroup effects, uncertainty and mismatch with the target operating conditions.
Trace continuation, deployment and scaling decisions against pre-defined stop criteria and identify whether sunk cost, schedule, sponsorship or visibility overrode the evidence.
Execute and independently review a complete scoped absence test covering every material AP-A2 mechanism for the current decision and solution boundary.

antipattern_indicators: The use case starts with a predetermined AI solution
Progress continues despite poor outcome evidence

required_evidence.title: Decision chronology and solution-selection record
required_evidence.description: The AI mechanism was selected or committed before a technology-neutral problem, baseline and value hypothesis were established. Acceptance: Traces problem definition, procurement, technical selection, funding, metric design and approval dates. Identifies pre-commitments, incentives and assumptions that constrained alternatives. Boundary: An early AI hypothesis is not automatically solutionism when selection remains reversible and evidence-gated.

required_evidence.title: Baseline and alternatives integrity assessment
required_evidence.description: Non-AI or simpler alternatives were omitted, misrepresented or evaluated only after the AI choice was effectively fixed. Acceptance: Reviews feasible process, rules, deterministic automation, data, human and no-change options. Uses the same outcome, scale, cost, risk and lifecycle assumptions for each option. Boundary: A technically inferior alternative may be legitimately rejected when the rationale and evidence are current.

required_evidence.title: Metric and causal-chain integrity analysis
required_evidence.description: Usage, activity, delivery, benchmark or publicity metrics substitute for attributable outcome value. Acceptance: Maps each reported metric to the desired outcome, baseline, owner, threshold and causal assumptions. Identifies metric changes, omitted costs, displaced work and unmeasured affected-person outcomes. Boundary: A leading activity metric is valid only when its causal role and outcome validation are explicit.

required_evidence.title: Comparative result, cost and risk record
required_evidence.description: Representative evidence is negative, inconclusive or incomplete while positive claims omit material cost, risk, subgroup or control-burden results. Acceptance: Preserves complete pre-defined metrics, failures, uncertainty, comparator results, costs and limitations. Uses the current system version and representative operating conditions. Boundary: A failed experiment supports learning and is not value theatre unless decision claims or progression disregard the result.

required_evidence.title: Continuation and stop-criteria trace
required_evidence.description: Funding, deployment, continuation or scale proceeded despite unmet or absent decision thresholds. Acceptance: Compares pre-defined thresholds with the evidence and actual decision. Records any exception, accountable authority, constraints, expiry and reassessment duty. Boundary: An authorized bounded learning experiment may continue after inconclusive results when its purpose and limits remain explicit.

required_evidence.title: Scoped absence-test package
required_evidence.description: A current, executed and independently reviewed assessment covers all material AP-A2 failure mechanisms. Acceptance: Covers decision chronology, technology-neutral problem, baseline, alternatives, value metrics, total cost, risk, representative results and stop-criteria enforcement. Identifies scope, versions, decision period, results, limitations and independent reviewer. Boundary: Document presence, project approval, successful delivery or lack of criticism is never TESTED_ABSENT.

sufficiency: Trace each value claim to its metric and decision record; if usage grew while the evaluation missed its agreed outcome threshold, preserve both records and verify what the decision owner did.
When capability A2 is NOT_SATISFIED or UNKNOWN and AP-A2 evidence is unavailable, AP-A2 remains UNKNOWN rather than defaulting to CONFIRMED_PRESENT or TESTED_ABSENT.
Use the current solution, target scale, cost structure, alternatives and decision authority.
Repeat the absence test after material change, metric redesign or continued use beyond the decision expiry.
Operational evidence must cover the period and scale on which the value claim depends.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: Silence, absence of complaints, missing incident logs, or unexecuted discovery never establishes TESTED_ABSENT; TESTED_ABSENT requires a current, executed, and independently reviewed absence test across decision chronology, non-AI comparison, outcome metrics, and continuation decisions for the current version.
false_positive_guards: A time-boxed feasibility exercise that starts with a candidate AI tool while leaving adoption undecided—with baseline, comparison, and stopping conditions governing the next decision—is not AP-A2.
Do not label a bounded exploratory sandbox pilot as AP-A2 when adoption is explicitly undecided, baseline comparison is scheduled, and stop criteria are enforced.
Do not treat failed trial outcomes as AP-A2 when governance promptly halts progression in accordance with pre-defined stop criteria.
prohibited_inferences: Never infer TESTED_ABSENT from silence, lack of complaints, missing incident logs, or unexecuted discovery.
Never infer AP-A2 CONFIRMED_PRESENT solely from capability A2 being NOT_SATISFIED or UNKNOWN.
Never infer realized value from login counts, prompt volume, or executive announcements.

required_artifacts: Decision chronology and technology-neutral problem formulation
Complete comparative result, cost, risk and impact evidence
Independent review and residual limitation statement

conditions: Block consequential deployment or scale when the anti-pattern is confirmed or materially present.
Constrain activity to a bounded learning experiment when the problem, alternatives, metrics or value evidence remain UNKNOWN.
Block continuation when agreed stop criteria are met and no accountable, time-bounded exception is formally approved.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1 (January 2023) MAP 1.4 (p. 31); MAP 3, MAP 3.1 & MAP 3.2 (p. 32); MANAGE 1.1, MANAGE 2.1 & MANAGE 2.4 (p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Voluntary risk-management guidance grounding evaluation of business-value definition, benchmarked benefit/cost examination, inclusion of viable non-AI alternatives, and disengagement or deactivation when outcomes miss intended objectives.

finding_definitions.title: AI was effectively selected before a technology-neutral problem, baseline and value hypothesis were established
Alternative and proportionality assessment is absent, biased or ceremonial
Activity, adoption or technical metrics substitute for measurable outcome value
Negative, inconclusive, cost, risk or impact evidence is omitted or overridden while progression continues
Absence of AI-first solutionism or value theatre is not established by a scoped current test
